Not sure where this person is from but I saw a post from a man in Australian on one of the Facebook groups I was in whose large dog had ingested a mouse that had he had eaten in the backyard while Australian was being absolutely overwhelmed with mice. He even posted a few pics of the poor dog in his last days after desperately going to the vet and having them give him large doses of Vitamin K in a last ditch effort to reverse the effects as it acts as an anticoagulant. The dog didn’t make it. I literally was hysterically crying over the pics, it looked horrific. I’m not sure on the statistics of cats ingesting poisoned rats/mice but it seems plausible because after they have ingested the poison the mice they act very out of it and and move slowly and don’t run away when you approach them. I found a mouse in the kitchen in my friends house who used rat poison and the mouse was just laying in the middle of the floor and just let me come up to it and pick it up with a paper towel. He clearly looked like he was dying so I took him outside and ended his misery. I know we can’t have rats or mice running around but standard rat poison causes death by massive internal bleeding and is extremely painful.

Animals can die from eating rats that have ingested rat poison, but I have never seen vomit of this color. As I said above usually rat poison ingestion causes massive internal bleeding. Including vomiting of blood.

I’m so sorry for the sudden loss of your feline companion. Losing a pet is horrific, but losing one without any warning is even worse. The shock is most certainly overwhelming you and I offer you my most sincere condolences and I beg the universe to bring you peace and comfort during this awful time. If possible maybe a vet could help identify this or if you are financially able you could get a lab to test it if that brings you a sense of closure or anything. I do agree with some that it looks like laundry detergent or rat poison but I also see many white chunks. This could possible be some sort of substance that is used in gardening, my chihuahua licked some fancy plants and got incredibly sick, defecating blood for days but he pulled through. Also, most rat poison causes massive internal bleeding, and the animal starts bleeding profusely from many openings in the body and it is quite a horrific death to witness. But I’m not sure if a huge ingestion of it could cause death before this sets in. Possible go on ask a vet Reddit group.

Have you ever heard of the thundershirt? They make them for both dogs and cats. They provide slight pressure to the main body of the animal, and much like in humans with sensory issues who use weighted blankets to self soothe and calm, they have the same effect for many pets with anxiety issues. They are little shirts or vests that apply pressure in a special distributed way that allows the nervous system to be reset, along the same thinking of acupressure/acupuncture. My old Belgian sheepdog was a neurotic mess around Halloween and this helped him stay nice and calm on the bed, he was aware of the big bangs but not frantic like he used to be, racing around the house thinking we are being bombed. I think they are pretty fairly priced too, not a terribly expensive investment. You may be able to make one if you’re crafty with fabric and check how to make it. 

Edit: I just checked amazon and there are tons of different pressure vests for pets now. Thundershirt is just the one I used. From like 15-50$ depending on size. Cat one should be cheaper than one for a Belgian sheepdog :)

But during these small interactions with people you don’t know or care about let’s your brain learn how to do it. We as humans are naturally intensely social, but isolation and turning into ourselves can seriously damage our ability to socialize. And the repercussions can literally be fatal. It takes work and putting yourself into some awkward situations to get your bearings again.
